W2 (empirical), after E041. Tip is E036: 5.314 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0-2. Fresh seeds 13-22 (E038) gave 0.7525, so the population mean is about 0.752. The 0.75 bar has about 0.2 pp of headroom, and the 0.753 gate on seeds 0-2 is a coin flip for the tip itself.

Mechanisms, each tied to its experiments:
1. Epoch dial: about 5% of time per 0.5 epoch, for 0.0-0.25 pp (E020, E023, E027). E034 stacked the freeze with +0.5 epoch and saved 0.40 s versus E027 at about 0 pp.
2. EMA (+0.97 pp, E005) and Muon (+0.66 pp, confounded, E006) are in the tip. More than 10 time-neutral boosters failed (E025, E029, E030, E032, wd, LS). Averaging, LR shape and wd sit at a flat optimum within about 0.2 pp, so the tip's recipe knobs are exhausted.
3. Time tracks pixels. Early low resolution is nearly free up to about 30% at 20 px (E026, E033). Pushing further failed: E040 (40/0/30/30) cost 0.06 pp and missed the gate. E041 (uniform step trim of 12 steps) cost 0.2 pp, so any trim of the 28/32 px phases is costly.
4. Backward truncation on memory-bound large maps was the best lever (E028, E034, E036). E037 (freeze at 60%) saved 0.25 s but cost 0.38 pp. E039 (BN folding) saved about 0.03 s and lost 0.15 pp. The stem is nearly exhausted.
5. Noise: identical code is bit-identical. Any change to step count or RNG use reshuffles the 3-seed mean by about 0.2 pp. Time noise is about 0.5%.

Misses: truncation savings were larger than I modelled. Time-neutral accuracy gains were over-predicted. Accuracy fell whenever training signal was cut. The tip is near the Pareto front, and any further trim needs an accuracy refund paid in epochs, which eats the saving.

Unsure: whether bandwidth-bound levers transfer to the PCIe judge. Also unsure whether any trim can clear 0.753 on seeds 0-2.

forecasts.reason: Diagnostic with no recipe change. Tip numbers are unchanged (bit-identical). The profile likely shows the non-GEMM share is large on the 31x31 maps.
A partial freeze at 60% should save a bit less than E037 (0.25 s) and cost less accuracy. It probably still misses the 0.753 gate.
Moving the freeze from 75% to 70% saves about 0.05 s. The cost is probably within noise, but the gain is too small to be worth the gate risk.
Recomputing BN stats may add a little accuracy, but BN momentum is already adapted. The 3 forward batches cost about 0.03 s.
The 16 px start saves a little time, since small maps are inefficient. It risks a small accuracy loss, and the gate is hard.
A math-identical cleanup saves about 0.03 s on the mean. Accuracy is bit-identical to the tip.

cruxes: Is the tip's true population mean (about 0.752) enough to leave any room for further trims, or must an accuracy booster be found first?
Where does E037's 0.38 pp cliff come from: freezing before the 32 px phase, or total lost group-1 training signal?
Does batch size (1500 vs 2000) give accuracy cheaper than epochs?
